Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  217 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
3 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.25 -0.11 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 The Times of Israel says the American blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is 'ironclad,' per The Times of Israel; the claim has not been independently confirmed.

02 A Kuwait-flagged tanker was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 1, with five Indian nationals rescued; FM Bharat reports the vessel was Kuwait-flagged.

03 Al Jazeera reports oil tankers were attacked in the Hormuz strait, per the UK maritime agency; Saba, the Houthi-run Yemeni state news agency, claims seven tankers were targeted over five days.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the centre of active maritime conflict, with projectile strikes on commercial tankers continuing into early October. The most operationally significant development in this window is a statement attributed to US Defense Secretary Hegseth declaring the American blockade of the strait 'ironclad,' carried by The Times of Israel; no other source in this feed carries that claim. On October 1, a Kuwait-flagged tanker was struck by a projectile in the strait, with five Indian nationals rescued, per FM Bharat and TheWire.in, among others; no major wire in this feed carries the story independently. Al Jazeera reports that the UK maritime agency has recorded attacks on oil tankers in the strait. Saba, the Houthi-run Yemeni state news agency, claims seven tankers were targeted over five days, a figure that should be treated as a claim from that outlet. Iraq's state tanker firm moved crude through the strait, per Investing.com. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $102.25, down 0.11% in the last session before the close, as of 23:49 UTC; futures are shut and that figure has not moved since close. Thirty-eight events were indexed across the past 24 hours, reflecting the sustained pace of incidents in and around the waterway. As of 23:50 UTC, 171 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.

Cite as
Straits, “Hormuz daily brief”, 3 Oct 2026 .
